items.title: The Rundown launches a Community AI Workflow Hub
points: A free hub where readers browse, submit, and learn practical AI workflows (step-by-step recipes for using AI tools to get a specific job done), built after survey feedback from hundreds of thousands of readers who wanted real workflows from everyday knowledge workers, not executives or influencers.
Solves a structural gap: 2M+ newsletter readers were sending in daily workflow submissions with no central place to find each other.
Workflows are searchable by problem-type and include the actual tools, steps, and prompts (the text instructions given to an AI model) so readers can implement them the same day.
Submitting takes 5 steps, with AI-assisted backend formatting that keeps entries raw and unfiltered rather than polished.
One top submission per day is featured to 2M+ readers with a LinkedIn attribution link, creating recruiter, founder, and networking exposure for contributors.
Rules: submit only workflows you actually run, show the 'how' rather than just impressive outcomes, and no spam or drive-by promotion — enforced by full-time moderators working 24/7.
Participation is free and requires only a Rundown University account; the interface is deliberately simple, with no complex channels or extra features.

issues.subject: 🤝 A new home for real AI workflows

headlines: The Rundown launched a Community AI Workflow Hub after reader surveys showed demand for real workflows from everyday users rather than executives and influencers.
The new hub lets users browse, submit, and learn practical AI workflows in 5 simple steps, with daily featured submissions promoted to 2M+ newsletter readers.
Featured workflows are searchable by problem-type and include actual tools, prompts, and steps that can be implemented immediately.
Top daily submissions get promoted with LinkedIn attribution, creating networking and job opportunity potential for contributors.
The hub is free and requires only a Rundown University account to participate.

sections.title: 1. Community AI Workflow Hub Launch
points: Founded after survey feedback from hundreds of thousands of readers requesting more practical AI workflows from real knowledge workers rather than hype-focused content.
Solved a structural problem: 2M+ newsletter readers with daily workflow submissions, but no centralized place for them to find each other.
Intentionally designed as a simple browsing interface without complex channels or features, prioritizing ease of discovery and immediate implementation.

sections.title: 2. Hub Features and Submission Process
points: Users browse workflows by problem-type, access actual tools/steps/prompts, and can implement the same day without complex navigation.
Submissions require 5 simple steps with AI-assisted backend formatting to keep content raw and unfiltered rather than polished.
Community moderators work 24/7 to prevent spam and maintain submission quality standards.
Every day, one top submission is featured in the newsletter reaching 2M+ readers, with a LinkedIn link driving potential recruiter and founder attention to the contributor.

sections.title: 3. Submission Guidelines and Community Standards
points: Workflows must be ones the submitter actually runs—rough-but-real implementations are preferred over polished theoretical concepts.
Posts must show the 'how' with concrete tools, steps, and prompts rather than just highlighting impressive outcomes.
Spam and drive-by promotion are prohibited with enforcement by full-time community moderators.
